text: A Train Wreck, Toward the Light, and Someone's There are the first quests in Chapter 11, "Haunted", in Final Fantasy VII Remake, taking place in the Train Graveyard. Cloud Strife, Aerith Gainsborough, and Tifa Lockhart make their way to the Train Graveyard, and must then find a way to the Sector 7 Slums.

The Adamant Turtle is an enemy from Final Fantasy Mystic Quest. It attacks with fire, and is weak to axe-type attacks. As Reuben's weapon is an axe, Adamant Turtle can easily be slain by him along with the player's own axe. Adamant Turtle has two phases. The first phase has it rear its head back in a menacing manner. The second phase has it tucked into its shell.

Adamantine Blade, also known as Diamond Sword, is a Sky Mantra ability in Final Fantasy Tactics, available for the skyseer's job. It charges a spell that deals minor wind-elemental damage to units within the effect radius, capable of striking multiple times per tile. The action ability must be learned by expending JP earned for the skyseer job. The only playable skyseer is Rapha Galthena. Other abilities that deal wind damage include the geomancer's Wind Slash & Wind Blast, and the netherseer's Nether Blade, which is Adamantine Blade's counterpart.

The Adaman Hat is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a late game hat that everyone but Steiner and Freya can equip. It teaches Gamble Defense, which randomizes the character's Defense in damage calculation but their Defense can be higher than their base, and HP+20%. It nullifies Thunder damage to the wearer.

The Adaman Vest is an early to mid game light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX that everyone but Steiner and Freya can wear. It teaches Bird and Stone Killer, which improve damage against birds and flying enemies, as well as stone-type enemies, respectively. The Adaman Vest halves Fire damage to the wearer. Like many equipment pieces in Final Fantasy IX, the Adaman Vest is named after the light armor piece of the same name from Final Fantasy Tactics.

Aern are humanoid in appearance, each one has a particular job, and while the job cannot be discerned by their name, the abilities, characteristics, and weapon speak for themselves. Each Aern also has a special TP ability based on which weapon it is wielding. The Aerns exhibit some rather unique abilities. Aerns occasionally have blue crystalline "wristbands" appear for up to 30 seconds before being removed. They will continue to apply and remove their wristbands even while asleep. When equipped, the Aern receives an increase in attack power and speed. Of additional interest is the fact that about 40% of the time, Aerns will Reraise to full HP and MP a few seconds after they are defeated—and some, like the Dark Knight Ix'aern, may Reraise multiple times before being defeated for good. Adventurers should be careful, as a reraised Aern will automatically attack the person/party that defeated it if within range. Aerns may drop items after conceding defeat including organs and Luminian tissue. If Aerns drop items after defeat they will not Reraise.

Aero+ is a wind-elemental magic ability in Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII exclusive to the Woodland Walker garb. It is a unique version of the Aero spell that casts Aerora for its finale attack.

Agent is a job class exclusive to Al-Cid Margrace in Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. He wields a gun and has several abilities that only affect female characters. Al-Cid cannot change into other jobs, so he is restricted to Reconnaissance and Items. He has no access to reaction or passive abilities.
The Air Force, otherwise known as AirForce, is a boss in Final Fantasy VI flanked by Laser Gun and Missile Bay. It attacks the party during their first flight to the Floating Continent.

The Airship and Hiryuu glitch is a glitch in the SNES version of Final Fantasy V, which is extremely harmful, more so for the airship than the wind drake. The glitch involves landing the airship or the wind drake on the tile where the entrance to Ghido's Cave is located in the merged world (unlike other caves in the game, the wind drake can fly directly above the entrance). Doing so will result, as with the black chocobo glitch, in the player never being able to retrieve the airship or the wind drake, making it impossible to complete the game since the airship is required to enter the Interdimensional Rift. The glitch was fixed in the PlayStation and subsequent releases by making it impossible to land on top of the entrance, even though the wind drake can still fly directly above the tile where the entrance is located. it:Glitch Aeronave ed Hiryu

The airship glitch in Final Fantasy VI allows the player to use the Blackjack airship early, potentially as early as entering the overworld for the first time after leaving Narshe. It requires the player to play from whichever point they want to use the airship all the way to the Floating Continent without saving. It is known to work with the original SNES and Super Famicom versions, but may also be possible on the PlayStation and GBA ports. The glitch is triggered by saving on the overworld at whatever point the player wants to access the airship, and then continuing as normal without saving. The player must cross the Floating Continent and return to the Blackjack, fly around without landing, then return to the Floating Continent and trigger a Game Over there. When the game resumes, the player returns to the point they last saved, except they will be on board the airship. Because the airship is acquired through glitching, its use comes with many limitations. The interior cannot be accessed, and the player can only land once before the airship becomes inaccessible, depending on when in the story the glitch is triggered. It's recommended to land near Zozo if one intends to complete the game, as it's close to where the player would first acquire the airship normally, and the furthest point in the story where the game can be completed using the glitch, as the airship becomes accessible again after Setzer is named. An airship theme is a recurring type of motif in the Final Fantasy series. It plays when the party travels in an airship around the world map. Original versions of airship themes appear in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call with a special field animation. __TOC__

The Airship Revolution (1771) is an event in Final Fantasy IX that took place 29 years before the events of the game. Resolving a series of conflicts that had lasted for centuries, the Airship Revolution brought about a peace treaty between the Mist Continent nations.
Airship Interior is a location in World of Final Fantasy. It is first visited in Chapter 21, "Chaos in Grymoire".

Aletap Rumors are additional information about the various equipment, i.e. weapons and armor, in Final Fantasy XII as told by a third party. More often than not, the rumors will provide the player with hints as to what materials are needed to have the subject of the rumor made at the bazaar. An Aletap Rumor is gained by defeating a set number of one kind of enemy, in the same manner as Sage Knowledge. Aletap Rumors are always signed with the name and profession of the third party telling the rumor.
All Aboard for Sector 4 is a quest in Chapter 5, "Dogged Pursuit", in Final Fantasy VII Remake. Cloud Strife, Barret Wallace, and Tifa Lockhart board the train to attack Mako Reactor 5.

Amber Bahamut is one of the two enemies accompanying Jet Bahamut in the final battle in Final Fantasy XIII-2. Amber Bahamut somewhat resembles the left half of Orphan from Final Fantasy XIII. They share similar coloring, identical arm positions, and excel in magic and healing spells.
Ancient Weapon is a Notorious Monster from Final Fantasy XI: Rise of the Zilart. It is spawned alongside Legendary Weapon for Zilart Mission 5: Headstone Pilgrimage.

The Ancient Aroma is an add-on in Final Fantasy IX for female party members. It teaches Odin's Sword, which allows Dagger's Odin to deal damage to enemies. The Ancient Aroma gives a bonus to the wearer's Strength when they level up with it equipped. It strengthens the wearer's Shadow damage but makes them weak to Holy. Many equipment pieces in Final Fantasy IX allude to Final Fantasy Tactics and Ancient Aroma may be part of this group, as it appears to be a perfume; Tactics was the first game in the Final Fantasy series to have perfumes as equippable accessories.

The Arcane Scepter is a weapon for Aerith in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It provides the Fleeting Familiar ability, which summons a fairy that provides supplemental damage. The Arcane Scepter's unlocks provide an increase to Aerith's normal attack damage, while being overall balanced.

The Armored Weapon, also known as Lethal Wpn and LethaWpn, is an enemy from Final Fantasy VI. Despite being weak to -elemental spells, players should be wary of their high magic defense and preset reflect status.

Argento is a Tsviet who plays a minor role in the Online Mode of Dirge of Cerberus -Final Fantasy VII-. Unlike other Tsviets, Argento is not much of a fighter. Instead, she acts as an instructor and observer, embodying the phrase "strength hidden in weakness." Argento wears a predominately white version of the uniform worn by Deepground Commanders; a crownlike visor appears on her head, and an eyepatch covers her right eye. Argento wields a black and silver SOLDIER broadsword with an engraved hilt. It was she who designed the other Tsviets' weapons. Argento took great care in doing so; she ensured that each weapon bore a unique color. During a conversation with Shelke, Argento reveals her hatred of the Restrictors, whom she and the other Tsviets plan to overthrow. Argento presents a pair of pistol swords to Weiss the Immaculate after he is set free; the man uses them to battle Rosso the Crimson and Azul the Cerulean, as well as to kill the leader of the Restrictors. This secures the freedom of Argento and the other Tsviets. Argento and the other Tsviets are present when the player character dies after receiving a fatal wound from the leader of the Restrictors. It is unknown what became of Argento after this.

:This article covers the recurring armor and Accessory type known as Armlets. For the page that covers Rings as an Accessory, see Rings. Armlets , Bracers , and Bangles, are a recurring type of armguards in the Final Fantasy series, which also appear as accessories in some titles. They are often used by melee and magical-based jobs that cannot equip their counterpart, the gauntlets, like the Monk, the White Mage, and the Black Mage. Examples of recurring armlets in the series are the Power Armlet, Silver Armlet, and Mythril Armlet.

Armor Construct is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. They will counter any magic attack by using Self-Destruct, so it is advised to only use physical attacks on them. They are not powerful, but the player should not cast Berserk on them, as it will only make them much more difficult to defeat. The Armor Construct the player faces as a "monster-in-a-box" drops a Ribbon, and this is only accessible in "The Planet Eater" episode. In this same episode it can also be fought in the X-shaped peninsula on the southeast of Kaipo for the high-tier axes such as Ogrekiller, Poison Axe, and the game's second strongest axe Rune Axe.
Armored Assassin is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought during the main quest Express Train for Trouble. It is a magitek trooper who fights with two swords.
The Armor of Oppression is a Trial in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius found in the Chamber of the Fallen. Players face the Iron Giant as a boss, with a difficulty of 10★.

.]] Artifact equipment is the job-specific equipment in Final Fantasy XI and Final Fantasy XIV obtained through a series of quests. Typically the armor sets are inspired by early-franchise depictions of traditional jobs, although many sets are of original design. The player community has adopted "AF" as the abbreviation for Artifact gear and its variants, a phrase that has carried over to Final Fantasy XIV. Though the higher-level sets are referred to by NPCs and the UI as "Relic" and "Empyrean" equipment, the players have taken to calling them "AF2 and 3" or "AFv2 and v3". With the possibility in Final Fantasy XI to rapidly power-level a character through Abyssea, many players opt not to quest for Artifacts because they become obsolete relatively early. Similarly, Artifacts are often treated as a cosmetic/glamour item by players in Final Fantasy XIV due to how swiftly the Artifact tends to be replaced, though in this case there are no specific quests to perform beyond that of normal job-progression. Level 50 Artifacts can be entrusted to an NPC for storage in both games, allowing collectors to keep their inventory open. Level 60, 70 and 80 Artifacts may not be stored in a similar manner.
.]] Assault Gun is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series, commonly used by Barret Wallace.

The Assist system is a gameplay feature introduced in Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy that allows for a fighter to call an ally into battle to perform an attack. It is designed to oppose EX Mode as a game mechanic—accessories that enhance Assists negatively affect EX Mode and vice-versa, and EX Break and Assist Break allow one mechanic to cancel out the other.
.]] Assault Targe is a recurring accessory or armor in the Final Fantasy series.
The Astral Bracers is an arm armor exclusive to the 3D versions of Final Fantasy III. It provides 47 Defense, 20 Magic Defense, +10 Mind, and +10 Intellect. It can be used by the Summoner class.

The Astral Cuff is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It is by far the best magic defense armor, providing +20 to and +124 to , but has no materia slots. Its complement is the iron maiden.

Attack Power , also known as Attack, AP, Battle Power, Bat.Pwr, Weapon Power, and P-Attack, is a recurring stat in the series that boosts the strength of physical attacks. It is typically associated with Strength, and is often a counterpart which is boosted by weapons rather than levels.
.]] Aurora Rod is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series, associated with Aerith Gainsborough.

Auto-weapon ability materia is a in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. It allows a non-controlled ally to use the weapon abilities mapped to a shortcut without player input. These abilities use ATB, meaning the party members will consume ATB charges on their own. A counterpart for unique abilities, , exists.

Back Amongst Friends, Blocked Road, and Clear the Way are quests in Chapter 11, "Haunted", in Final Fantasy VII Remake, taking place in the Train Graveyard. After traveling through a maintenance facility in the graveyard, Cloud Strife, Aerith Gainsborough, and Tifa Lockhart look for a way back to the Sector 7 Slums.
Bafsk is a town from Final Fantasy II, used as the construction site for the Palamecian Dreadnought.

The Bafsk Sewers are a dungeon from Final Fantasy II. They serve as a passage to the part of town where the Dreadnought is being built. Firion and his allies attempt to make their way through the sewers to stop the Dreadnought's completion, but they are too late: the Dreadnought is already complete. The Dark Knight and Borghen taunt Firion and then take off to go attack the towns where the rebels are located.

Baguba Port is a town from Final Fantasy Tactics Advance, specifically a moogle town. This town serves as a port for every trade ship in Ivalice, most notably, airships. This is one of two towns, the other being Muscadet, in which there is no other function than the Pub or the Shop. When going to the town for the first time, this is also where Marche meets Nono, Montblanc's younger brother. Out of the five towns, Baguba Port is the fourth town located. It is also the home of the clan "White Kupos", the primarily moogle clan fought as part of the Clan League (after the Brown Rabbits are defeated).

The Bad Rap Sample is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII. It appears alongside Hojo in the first battle against him on the Sister Ray at the end of "Mako Cannon Rampage". It is summoned together with Poodler Sample. It may use its Whip attack twice in one turn, while its Evil Poison attack always inflicts Darkness on one character. The samples cannot be defeated permanently, as Hojo will simply revive them, so it is better to ignore them and concentrate solely on the scientist himself.
Bakshin, the Unstoppable, is an obtainable character from King's Knight -Wrath of the Dark Dragon-. His pastime and talent is Sword Training.

The Balaclava is a mid-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 12 and HP by 90, and uniquely for a light armor hat, also gives +1 to the wearer's Strength. Its stats are a bit of a jump up from the previously available light armor hat, Horned Hat.

Base Soldier appears as a blue G-Soldier in Final Fantasy VIII. It accompanies the Base Leader in a boss fight, using a standard sword attack, as well as magic attacks when ordered. The party can put them to sleep while drawing and casting Blizzard or Blizzara.

The Baron Warrior, also known as the Baron Marine or Fighter, is an enemy in Final Fantasy IV. They only attack when ordered to back their Captain. A few uses of Kick and Dark Wave will dispatch them. However, the player should focus on killing the Captain first to earn more EXP.

The Bard Vest is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 15 Defense, 7 Magic Defense, 12% Evasion, and -6 Attack in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions it provides 32 Defense, 28 Magic Defense, +2 Mind, and +2 Agility. It can be used by the Onion Knight and Bard classes in all versions, and the Freelancer class in the 3D versions.
The Barrel Coat is a mid-ranked light armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's defense by 38 (Zodiac) or 30 (original), and HP by 360.

Battle Harness is an accessory in Final Fantasy XII that allows the wearer to counterattack normal enemy attacks with an attack with their equipped weapon, and can counter repeatedly if the enemy attack combos. How often the effect activates depends on the wearer's Speed stat. The harness also gives +2 to Strength.
.]] Battle Fork is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.

Basic Training: Enemy Parties is a guildhest in Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn. Set near Summerford in Middle La Noscea, the objective is to learn how to carefully deal with enemy parties without being overwhelmed.
The Beamer, also known as the Beam Cannon, is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV. It appears within the Giant of Babel and the Lunar Ruins.
The following is a list of armor used by the Turks from Before Crisis -Final Fantasy VII-. As in the original Final Fantasy VII, characters can only equip a single piece of armor.
Beestinger is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.
Belhelmel is an enemy in Final Fantasy VIII, commonly found on the Galbadian continent. It has a rotating blade around its face and its battle tactics change when its face changes.

.]] Bells , also called Handbells, are a recurring weapon type in the Final Fantasy series; they are often associated with Geomancers. For games with the classic row-based battle system, the power of bells remains unchanged when used from the back row. The bell weapons are associated with the Geomancer class, known as "feng shui knight" in Japanese. Feng shui is the Chinese studying of the direction, geography and/or weather to calculate the individual's fortune who resides or works in that place. Bells are used in the craft as instruments to dispel negative energy and stimulate positive energy, and that's why they are wielded as weapons by Geomancers.
Belial is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It has low Vitality. Using Costly Punch or Drain Blade is recommended. It has valuable items up for stealing.
.]] Behemoth Suit is a recurring armor piece in the Final Fantasy series. It originates from Final Fantasy VI as an animal suit for Strago Magus and Relm Arrowny.
The Birthday Suit is a joke enemy in Final Fantasy VI. A Cadet or Merchant becomes this enemy after Locke steals his clothes.

Biotechnological Weapon represent the pinnacle of ancient technological weaponry, these bizarre machines are among the most dangerous foes in all of Vana'diel. The biotechnological weapons fought in the Chains of Promathia mission "One to be Feared" were created by Nag'molada based on the original weapons that have remained lost in Al'Taieu since the Zilart's war with the wyrms ten thousand years ago. The Black Robes is a high-ranked mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 56 (Zodiac) or 38 (original), and Magick Power by 12 (Zodiac) or 10 (original), and improves the wearer's Dark damage by 50%. In the Zodiac versions, it also gives 5 Magick Resist (usually only gained from mystic headgear), and 66 MP. It is a contender for endgame gear for its good stats and Dark-potency property, especially against the superboss Yiazmat. Black Robes is the dark counterpart of the Holy-boosting White Robes whose bazaar set requires one of the same items; for best efficiency to unlock both sets simultaneously, the player can make use of the "bazaar glitch".
The Blade Dancer, formerly called SoulDancer and SoulDncr, is an enemy in Final Fantasy VI.

The Blade Biter in Final Fantasy Tactics Advance is a purple turtle-like monster with extremely high Defense and high Attack stats. Being a stronger version of normal Toughskin, it has the capability to permanently destroy weapons and unleash a devastatingly powerful attack when at critically low HP. Melee attackers should take care not to get their weapons crushed, especially if they are rare or one of a kind. Like its lesser cousin, it also possesses the Resonate ability to further decrease the usefulness of most physical weapons. Unlike most monsters, the Blade Biter has no abilities that can be learned as Blue Magic.
Blade Dragon is a boss encountered at the end of Palom's Challenge Dungeon in Final Fantasy IV: The After Years.

Blaster Mine is a Mix ability in Final Fantasy X, usable by Rikku as her Overdrive. It deals a single hit of approximately 1,100 damage to all enemies and attempts to inflict darkness, silence, and sleep for 3 turns at 150% accuracy. Status resistance values are subtracted from infliction chances, rather than multiplied by; thus, a 50% infliction chance is canceled out by a 50% resistance, rather than being reduced to 25%. Blaster Mine returns as a mix in Final Fantasy X-2, albeit in a weaker form.

The Bladed Staff is a weapon in Final Fantasy VII Remake for Aerith. It provides her the Lustrous Shield ability, a defensive ability that creates a stationary shield to block projectiles. The Bladed Staff focuses on improving Aerith's normal attacks by improving her critical hit rate tremendously.
Blade for the Heart is an Intersecting Wills chapter in Dissidia Final Fantasy Opera Omnia focusing on Edge and his companions.
Blind Dagger is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. It typically attempts to blind those it targets.

Boots , also called Shoes, are a recurring type of accessory and armor in the Final Fantasy series. They usually boost movement and jump stats in the new tactical games, but other than that, they can also enable different actions to the party and boost some stats. An example of recurring boots in the series are the Hermes Sandals.

The Bone Helm is a mid ranked heavy armor helm in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 26 (Zodiac) or 22 (original) and Strength by 6. It halves Dark damage on the wearer while making them weak to Holy damage.
The Bracers is an armor in the Final Fantasy 20th Anniversary version of Final Fantasy II. It provides 30 defense, -5% evasion, and 34% Magic Defense, and can only be used by Josef.

Break Arts are special moves in Vagrant Story that drain Ashley Riot's Hit Points. There are 40 Break Arts, four for each type of weapon, including bare fists. Ashley will not be able use a Break Art if it would reduce him below one HP.
Broadaxe ( or ) is a recurring axe in the Final Fantasy series. It is generally a weak axe that provides no special bonuses.

The Bronze Vest is an early game light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX that everyone besides Steiner and Freya can wear. It teaches Jelly, which immunizes against Petrify. The Bronze Vest provides a bonus to the wearer's Spirit stat when they level up with it equipped.
The Bunyip is an enemy on the Djose Highroad in Final Fantasy X. It is best to bring in Auron or Kimahri for the Piercing ability on their weapon in order to defeat it.

The buggy is a land vehicle in Final Fantasy VII and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. Using reinforced tires, it is capable of traversing terrain that could not be crossed on foot. The buggy is owned by Dio of the Gold Saucer. The buggy serves as one of the means of transportation on the world map in Final Fantasy VII, capable of crossing shallow waters and deserts on the western continent. The buggy serves as a replacement of a chocobo in the desert regions in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth.

.]] Bull Head is an enemy in Chapters 5, 9, and 10 of Dirge of Cerberus -Final Fantasy VII- that serves as the mobile barricade and riot shield for the Deepground. Although its health is low, its front armor can block all physical attacks except that of Gatling guns (Chapter 10). It can ram its enemies to knock them down, providing Deepground an opening to come for the kill. The Bull Head's weak point is the drum behind the red and white box. It is also vulnerable to magic.
Bulletproof Suit is a recurring piece of equipment in the Final Fantasy series, originating from Final Fantasy XV as equipment for imperial forces.

Caliginous Bracelet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has poor stats but three materia slots, two of them linked. It provides +5 to and . It is good to equip to if the player wants the materia slots.

The Cannon Head is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It has high Vitality, Attack, Spirit, and Magic stats and is immune to Lightning. Gravity is a good starter followed by other spells. Alternatively, dualcasting Energy works well.
from Final Fantasy VIII.]] A car is a recurring method of transportation in Final Fantasy games. Sometimes they do not appear as vehicles the player can use, but are still part of the game world.

The Carabini Mail is a late game heavy body armor in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. It teaches Auto-Regen, which allows the character to regenerate health over time mid battle. It gives bonuses to the wearer's Speed and Spirit when they level up with the mail equipped. Like many equipment pieces in Final Fantasy IX, the Carabini Mail is based on an equipment piece from Final Fantasy Tactics.

The Carry Armor is a boss from Final Fantasy VII fought in the Underwater Reactor during "Clash in the Deep Sea". Reno uses it to delay the party while he escapes on a Shinra submarine with the Huge Materia. It is a machine with its Left Arm and Right Arm cranes that can disable party members by picking them up. Carry Armor drops the God's Hand weapon for Tifa. Fighting Carry Armor also makes Yoshiyuki become unavailable in Rocket Town if not already obtained.
Cavalier is an enemy in Final Fantasy Dimensions. It can be fought on the Warship.

The Chanter's Djellaba is a low to mid-ranked mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 15 (Zodiac) or 14 (original), Magick Power by 4, and—unusually for mystic armor headgear—Vitality by 5. In the Zodiac versions, it also gives 35 to MP.

Chain Bangle is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has excellent stats for a balanced armor piece, providing +50 to and , and it has four materia slots, all of them linked. It is a great equipment piece to equip on anyone.
A charged item (also enchanted items, dispensing items) is a type of weapon or armor/clothing in Final Fantasy XI, which gives a beneficial status effect, useful items, or a "costume".
Chaos Mace may refer to: *The weapon from Final Fantasy XII. *The weapon from Final Fantasy Record Keeper.

The Chaperon is a high-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 46 (Zodiac) or 40 (original), and HP by 600. Unlike its preceding light armor headgear, the Chaperon does not boost any other stat. However, it does excel in the light armor headgear stats in giving a good amount of magick resistance and HP.

The Chuse Tank is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII that resembles a seahorse. It can be fought during AVALANCHE's mission to destroy Mako Reactor 5 on the Lower Sector 4 Plate, the location before the player actually reaches the reactor. Chuse Tank is also a possible encounter in the Battle Square opening round before the player obtains the Tiny Bronco. In the Battle Square it has enhanced stats with double the normal HP and 25% higher Attack and Magic Attack.

Chronos, also known as the Cronos, is an enemy from Final Fantasy III that can be encountered in the Cave of Shadows. It divides when hit by a weapon other than a Dark Blade or not inflicted with Paralysis. It is therefore recommended to bring Ancient Swords to combat these enemies. They are moderately powerful, as is the case with all of the other enemies in the cave.

The Chromed Leathers is a light armor in Final Fantasy XII that slightly boosts the wearer's defense and HP. It is the second weakest light armor and basic equipment, Balthier and Fran starting out with it already equipped.
Chunak is a character of War of the Visions: Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. Known as the Veracious Blade Demon, he is a member of Jayden Rundall's personal guard, Vanum.

Chthonian Armlet is a piece of armor in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It has one set of linked materia slots and two single slots, and provides +42 to and . It is a good armor piece with balanced defense, and its efficacy is enhanced when the equipper also wears Gozu drive (increases damage dealt proportional to wearer's current HP) or Mezu drive (increases damage dealt inversely proportional to character's current MP). When coupled with the drives, it can be one of the best armor pieces in the episode, and is suitable for the superboss encounters. When active with a drive, the armlet glows red (Gozu) or blue (Mezu) in the menu.

The Cleric's Robes is a mid to high-ranked mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 50 (Zodiac) or 37 (original), and Magick Power by 9. In the Zodiac versions, it also gives 70 MP.

The Coal Train is a vehicle in Final Fantasy VII. It travels travels along a track that leads from the mako reactor in Mt. Corel to North Corel. The trains are used to transport a Huge Materia during the game's events.

Clothing, also known as Clothes in the PlayStation version, is the weakest light body armor piece in Final Fantasy Tactics. Clothes can be equipped by all job classes except for knights (including almost all special knights), dragoons, samurai, mimes, and the dragonkin.

Combinations are special effects in Dissidia Final Fantasy and Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy. By equipping specific armor and weapons together, special properties are bestowed on the wearer. Each combination requires equipping all three or four of the equipment pieces at once for the combination to take effect.
Cog Bangle is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has good stats and three materia slots, two of them linked. It provides +39 to and .
The Commander Crystal Armor is a boss in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers. It is part of the story sequence, and is fought in the Aerial Prison.

Companions are chocobos that will fight alongside the player in Final Fantasy XIV. Players can make their chocobos fill the role of a tank, healer, or damage dealer by putting the companion's skill points into the Defender, Healer, or Attacker skill trees. Companions cannot be used in instanced dungeons or duties, though beginning with patch 8.1, players will be able to form light parties with two players and their respective companion chocobos and enter instanced dungeons. Companions automatically adjust to the level of their player. Players can customize their chocobo with various bardings, cosmetic armour for chocobos. Players are also capable of dyeing their chocobo's feathers by feeding them different combinations of greens. To obtain a companion to summon into battle, players must obtain their company chocobo from their Grand Company by completing the My Little Chocobo quest at level 20, and then complete the quest at level 30. Afterward, players can summon the companion to fight alongside them by using ghysal greens sold by vendors. Once summoned, companions will receive a timer counting down until they need to leave again. This begins at 30 minutes of real time and can be increased to 60 by using another ghysal green. Chocobo companions can only accompany the player in non-instanced public field areas.
