.]] The Copperhead VTOL Tactical Transport Assault Craft (Copperhead for short) is a small, all-weather offensive transport appearing in Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within. Capable of carrying up to 10 people (8 seated, 1 pilot, 1 standing), the craft has a maximum speed of 720 km. A holographic tactical display is located in the ship's hold for troops to analyze and discuss field tactics while en-route to a location. The craft series is used frequently as drop ships during the movie for the Deep Eyes squadron; first while extracting Aki Ross from Old New York and a second time while touring and extracting the 7th spirit from the Tucson Wasteland. A Copperhead is also seen crashing during the Fall of the New York Barrier City as Aki, Dr. Sid, Gray and the Deep Eyes attempt to enter the military hangar while driving a Bandit Humvee.

The Coronet is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a late game hat that everyone but Steiner and Freya can equip. It teaches Man Eater, which allows the character to deal more damage to human enemies, and Return Magic, which allows the character to counterattack magic attacks with the same spell the enemy used. It nullifies Wind damage to the wearer and is used for synthesis.

Corneo Armlet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has two linked materia slots and provides +22 to and . It is good to equip to replace the Bronze Bangles Cloud and Tifa start with, and is better than the Shinra bangle.

The Cotton Shirt is a mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 4 and Magick Power by 1. In the Zodiac versions, it also gives 3 MP. It is the weakest mystic armor in the game and basic equipment.

The Cripshay is a rare enemy from Final Fantasy VII, which resembles a small stag beetle with humanoid features. It is fought in the Train Graveyard and in the third round of the Battle Square before the player obtains Tiny Bronco. When fought in the Battle Square its stats are enhanced with double the normal HP and its Attack and Magic Attack are increased by 25%. It only uses two physical attacks, which inflict minor damage. It has low HP, and thus poses little threat to the party. If the player is running low on HP at the Train Graveyard, finding and defeating these enemies can provide with a supply of Potions, which can also be stolen.

The Crazy Saw, referred to as Crazysaw in the BradyGames guide, is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII fought in the Sector 8 of Midgar during "Mako Cannon Rampage". Its Uppercut attack always inflicts Confusion, which can be dangerous, and they tend to deal a lot of damage, but as they are physical the Barrier ability and being in the back row can make the battle a lot easier. L4 Suicide works against them, leaving them open for morphing into Turbo Ethers. Otherwise, using a couple of powerful spells, like Trine, Magic Breath or Bolt3, is more than enough to defeat them.

Crazy Sword is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. Equipping the Safety Bit protects against the death effect from its Drill Attack. Strong magic materia, like Hell Thundaga or Energy, work well, as do powerful command materia, such as Costly Punch. Brutal, the accessory that raises Zack's damage limit becomes 99,999, is a rare steal from it.

Crimson Blade is an enemy from Vagrant Story, a footsoldier in the Order of the Crimson Blades. There are eleven different types that Ashley Riot may fight, each with unique stats. They respawn each time Ashley leaves and reenters the overall area they are in, or when he moves four 'rooms' away. The eleven types only differ in equipment and stats. Crimson Blades do not really require strategy beyond attacking whatever body part is the weakest. However, some Crimson Blades can cast low level magic, such as Herakles, Prostasia and weaker elemental magic. They are also not immune to any status ailments. The player should cast Degenerate and Tarnish on those that have these buffs.

The Cromwell is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII, fought in the Sector 8 area of Midgar during "Mako Cannon Rampage". They only know a single weak physical attack, but can attack twice in a single turn. The Enemy Skill Trine can be used to decimate groups of them, as they are weak to Lightning. They drop 8-inch Cannons, which are the most powerful physical attack item in the game, but by this point they are quite weak.

The critical hit bug is an ascended bug in the original Final Fantasy. Instead of loading a weapon's originally programmed critical hit rate, versions prior to the Dawn of Souls release load the weapon's index number. The practical effect of this is that critical hits are slightly less common than they were intended to be at the beginning of the game, and substantially more common than they were meant to be at the end of the game. Along with the Intelligence bug, the critical hit bug is the most game-changing bug in the original Final Fantasy. As of the Dawn of Souls release, the programmed critical hit rates of the original weapons are made equal to their index numbers, canonizing the bug as an intended feature. Newly introduced weapons in the Dawn of Souls and 20th Anniversary releases have their critical hit rates work as intended, unaffected by their index number. In the Pixel Remaster release, weapons retain their Dawn of Souls critical hit rates despite their index numbers being changed.

The Cross Helm is a mid game helmet in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. It teaches Devil Killer, which allows increased damage against devil type enemies, and MP Attack, which expends MP to increase the power of Attack, stacking with killer abilities. The Cross Helm gives a minor bonus to the wearer's Strength when they level up with it equipped. It is used for synthesis to make the ultimate helmet in the endgame. The Cross Helm in Final Fantasy IX is based on the "Close Helmet" from Final Fantasy Tactics.

The Crown of Laurels is a high-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 49 (Zodiac) or 42 (original), and HP by 680. Out of all the light armor headgear, it provides the second-best HP boost after the Dueling Mask's 800.
The Crystal Armor are crystal-powered mechanical enemies in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers.

CP is the main currency for events. The main use of CP is trading for event chests, which give weapons, and tier III (SR) weapon and ability scrolls, which cost 1500 CP each (250 the first time). Starting from the Final Fantasy VII main event, tier III (SR) summon scrolls became available for the same price as well. But that's not all CP is for. In the main part of most events, there is a CP ranking in addition to normal points rankings. CP ranking is on an individual basis only. The main part of each event, usually with a two week duration, give out rewards based on CP rankings, once during the middle (ie, after one week), and again at the end. The rewards are different each time and each event, but are usually contain extremely powerful weapons and summons, special backgrounds, weapon and ability scrolls, and large quantities of transmutation items. Ranking division is usually 1-10, 11-100, 101-500, 501-1000, 1001-2000, 2001-4000, 4001-7000, and 7001-10,000. 1-10 will usually get SR+ weapons, enough to limit boost to full; 11-100 will get SR+ weapons and some SR, enough to limit boost to full with some effort; and 101-500 will usually get some SR items. It is usually not possible to get all varieties of weapons without being in the top 100, and often not any weapon at all without being in the top 500. Scroll and transmutation item rewards also scale by rank. CP is obtained by fighting in brigade battles, and the amount depends almost entirely on damage dealt. From the Final

Cultsworn Lich is a Rare Game enemy found in Tomb of Raithwall in Final Fantasy XII. It is a stronger version of Lich. The player can steal the Loxley Bow from it. It is also fought optionally in the Zodiac versions' Trial Mode in Stage 9 alongside three Liches, where Cultsworn Lich appears by going to either the left or right side of the arena, and standing in the corner for a short period. Armor can be stolen from it at the trial: Golden Shield (common), Flame Shield (uncommon), and Lamia's Tiara (rare).

This is a list of the armor pieces in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". They are listed in the order they appear in the menu if sorted by type, the INTERmission-exclusives relegated to the end of the list. Armor functions similarly to the original Final Fantasy VII. Characters can equip a single piece of armor, alongside one accessory. The armor includes slots for materia, as well as boosts to attributes. Costs displayed here are the amount needed to purchase one, though what is available depends on the current chapter, and not all armor can be purchased. Selling prices are half of its cost.

Gear in Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis are alternate outfits obtained through various means. The most common is tied to the gacha; as the player pulls for weapons, they earn one or more stamps on a card toward guaranteed weapons and gear. Other methods include story progression, Gear Vouchers, and event exchanges. Each character can equip one set of gear in Battle, which boosts character stats, and an optional second set as a Skin, which changes appearance only. The "Recommended Party" auto-loadout feature attempts to select the best gear based on the parameters of the selected mission, such as elemental weaknesses and status effects, and other hidden determinations.

This is a list of the armor pieces in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. Armor functions similarly to Final Fantasy VII Remake. Party members can equip a single piece of armor, alongside one accessory. The armor includes slots for materia, as well as boosts to attributes.
This is a list of armor in Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings. Armor is sold in Tomaj's Sky Saloon shop aboard the Galbana.

In Final Fantasy V certain weapons, pieces of armor, and accessories have statuses associated with their use. Added statuses must not be confused with added abilities (e.g. Death via Assassin's Dagger). For armor and accessories, added statuses must not be confused with status immunities.

This is a list of shops throughout Spira in Final Fantasy X. The shops' stock tends to change after the party obtains the airship. A recurring type of shop is the Rin's Travel Agency that has many outposts in the world. O'aka XXIII is a traveling merchant whom the party can run into in various points.

All attacks in Final Fantasy XV are either physical or magical in nature. Each weapon type inflicts a specific type of damage. Royal arms have a hidden damage type that is not represented in the game by an icon.

The following is a list of hats in Final Fantasy XV: Episode Ardyn. They are equipped from the Gear menu and are the only form of equippable armor. New hats are bought from shops found around Insomnia while free-roaming. The yen needed to buy them is procured by selling treasures obtained from felled foes and found from the environment. Hats are classified as key items. ru:Шляпы Final Fantasy XV: Эпизод Ардин

Find Stamp, The Nose Knows, Check the Route, and Train Yard Security are quests in Chapter 5, "Dogged Pursuit", in Final Fantasy VII Remake that take place in Corkscrew Tunnel. Cloud Strife, Barret Wallace, and Tifa Lockhart travel through the Corkscrew Tunnel to find Mako Reactor 5. The group navigates by following graffiti of Shinra propaganda mascot Stamp.

Firebird Armlet is a piece of armor in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It has three single materia slots, and provides +46 to and . It is a good armor piece with balanced defense, but its main feature is that it revives the user once from KO, unless they were killed by an Instant Death attack or from 1 HP.

Firework Blade is a synergy ability in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, used by Cloud Strife with Aerith Gainsborough as a synergy partner. It costs three synergy charges each, deals magic damage to a foe, and boosts their limit level by 1, giving them new possible limit breaks. This can be boosted up to a limit level of 3 once this is unlocked from their folio. In the ability's animation, Cloud tosses his sword to the air, which Aerith empowers. Then, swinging Cloud's sword and Aerith's staff, they fire magic blasts at an opponent. Firework Blade has an ability power of 1135, and builds the stagger gauge by 10 (20 if the enemy is pressured). It has an interrupt power of 70, interrupt defense of 60, similar to a limit break, with the only exception that characters are still liable to incur damage during the execution of a synergy ability.

The Flash Hat is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a late game hat for Zidane, Vivi, Dagger, Eiko, and Amarant. It teaches Beast Killer, which allows the character to deal more damage to beast enemies, and Eye 4 Eye, which improves Counter. It strengthens the user's Thunder and Holy damage, and grants a small level up bonus to the wearer's Speed.
Force Bracelet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It has poor stats, providing +9 to and , but it has four materia slots, all of them linked.
Freesword's Bow is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.
Four Slots is an armor in Final Fantasy VII named after its Materia setup.
Fourth Bracelet is an armor in Final Fantasy VII. Fourth Bracelet is permanently missable.

Freezer Crab is an enemy type from Final Fantasy Mystic Quest. It is very weak to axe attacks. It has three phases. At first it raises its left claw in a menacing manner, but as it takes damage bubbles form around its mouth and its body is damaged.

Frost Armor is an ability in Final Fantasy XI. The ability is a level 28 Blood Pact: Ward for Shiva. It grants the Ice Spikes effect to all party members within an area of effect for a period of 90 seconds initially. Duration varies with Summoning magic skill, that exceeds level cap, but cannot exceed 3 minutes.

The Fuma Garb is a piece of armor exclusive to the 3D versions of Final Fantasy III. It provides 47 Defense, 39 Magic Defense, and +3 Agility. It can be used by the Onion Knight, Viking, Monk, Thief, Black Belt, and Ninja classes.
GIM47N is an enemy from Final Fantasy VIII. It is a Galbadian weapon commonly deployed with the army.
The Gaap is an enemy from Final Fantasy III. It can be found in either Falgabard Cave or Ancient Ruins and divides into two when hit by a weapon other than a Dark Blade.

G Paladin is an enemy from Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. He is a copy of Genesis Rhapsodos and closely resembles him. This Genesis lookalike has a strong Gunblade attack and can cast Curaga on himself. Graviga at the start of the fight, followed by a barrage of Hell Thundaga, works well. Continuous fast-and-hard attacks prevent the Paladin from casting Curaga.

G General is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It is a Genesis copy. G General frequently casts Barrier and MBarrier on itself. Dispel Blade can be used to get around the G General's defenses before following up with Hell Thundaga or Quake. Zack can attempt to steal an Iron Fist from the G General, vital to the creation of the powerful Costly Punch command materia.

The Gaia Vest is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 16 Defense, 8 Magic Defense, and 12% Evasion in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions it provides 35 Defense, 25 Magic Defense, and +3 Vitality. It can be used by the Onion Knight and Geomancer classes in all versions, and the Freelancer class in the 3D versions.
The Gas Ducter is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII fought during the Huge Materia events on the train from North Corel.

General's Tank is a boss in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It is fought together with the Support Machines. The player should defeat the Support Machines first. Although they pose little challenge, they can be an annoyance. When focusing on General's Tank, the player should land critical hits from its behind or spam Firaga and Hell Thundaga. With high Attack and Magic ratings, this fight should be easy to win.

The Gauntlets are endgame arm gear in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. They have the best physical Evasion of any gauntlet. The Gauntlets teach Cover, which allows the character protect allies from enemies' physical attacks. They give a bonus to the character's Speed stat when they level up with them equipped and halve damage from Fire, Earth, Water, and Wind.

The Genji Helmet is a the penultimate helmet in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. It teaches HP+20% and provides a bonus to the wearer's Magic when they level up with it equipped. Obtaining the whole Genji equipment set—Genji Helmet, Genji Armor, and Genji Gloves–earns the Path of the Samurai achievement/trophy in the latest versions.

Genji Glove is a relic in Final Fantasy VI. It allows the user to wield two weapons, one in each hand, meaning an attack will hit twice, once with each weapon. Genji Glove thus makes the wearer supremely powerful. The relic also provides a +5 Defense increase. Genji Glove notably makes for a great combination with the Master's Scroll, as the two relics allow a party member to attack eight times in one turn. The Genji Glove is part of the Genji equipment set that also includes the Genji Shield, Genji Armor, and the Genji Helm. Betting a Genji Glove at the Dragon's Neck Coliseum pits the player against a Demon Knight for the reward of a Thunder Shield.

Geometric Bracelet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It has poor stats but four materia slots, two of them linked. It provides +8 to and . Four is the most slots any armor has, but the player can find superior ones from the Drum.

The Ghost Ship is an enemy in Final Fantasy VII, encountered in the Underwater Reactor in the tunnel below the sea with a glass ceiling. It can also be encountered on the final round of the Battle Square after the player has acquired the Highwind and Cloud has rejoined the party. When fought in the Battle Square, it has enhanced stats with double the normal HP and its Attack and Magic Attack are increased by 25%. The Ghost Ship is notable for its Morph item, which can be used for the Kalm traveler quest.

Ghost Train is a boss from Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. It is fought in the Depths of the True Moon. Like in Final Fantasy VI, it fights the party in a back attack. Unlike its appearance in Final Fantasy VI, this boss cannot be defeated with a Phoenix Down or the Raise spell.
The Giant Stonebow is a bow in Final Fantasy XII. In the original version, its license costs 40 LP. In the Zodiac versions, its license costs 60 LP and it can be used by the Archer.

The Giant's Helmet is a high ranked heavy armor helm in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 38 (Zodiac) or 33 (original), HP by 150 and Strength by 8. Uniquely for a heavy armor helm, the Giant's Helm gives HP, usually a property reserved for light armor. It is metallic for the purposes of the boss battles against Vinuskar (though usually obtained after the boss is fought) and Ultima.

The Gigas Hat is a high-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 43 (Zodiac) or 38 (original), HP by 530, and—unusually for a light armor headgear—Magick Power by 2. It can thus be a good headgear for those who also use magick, such as for support healers.

The Gigas Chestplate is a high-ranked light armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's defense by 47 (Zodiac) or 38 (original), HP by 540, and—unusually for a light armor—Magick Power by 2. It can thus be a good armor for those who also use magick, such as for support healers.

The Goggle Mask is a mid-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 28 (Zodiac) or 25 (original), and HP by 270, and makes the wearer immune to Blind.

The Golden Hairpin is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is mid-to-top tier hairpin that everyone but Steiner and Freya can equip. It teaches Auto-Regen, which has the character intervally accumulate HP when in battle and is one of the best support abilities, and Loudmouth, which inoculates against Silence, an ailment that prevents the use of magic skills. It strengthens the wearer's Water damage and provides bonuses to Magic and Magic Evasion when the character levels up with the Golden Hairpin equipped. It is used in synthesis.

The Gold Helm is a mid game helmet in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. It teaches Clear Headed, which immunizes against Silence; Mental Break, which allows Steiner to lower an enemy's magic resistance; and Reis's Wind, which lets Freya bestow Regen to all allies. The Gold Helm gives a minor bonus to the wearer's Magic when they level up with it equipped. It is used for synthesis.

Gothic Bangle is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It has good stats and three single materia slots. It provides +33 to and . It is good to equip for balanced protection by the time it becomes available.
Grand Glove is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. It is often a low-ranked knuckle that provides no special bonuses.

Gray Coeurl is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. An occasional encounter, it will use Blaster to either Paralyze or KO a party member. It appears in Kain's Tale and The Crystals and they are the enemies that drop Gray Tails. __NOTOC__
The Great Helm, also known as Iron , is a basic helmet in Final Fantasy. It can be used by Warrior, Knight, and Ninja to provide 5 defense and 5 weight.

Grenade Combatant is an enemy with the appearance of an ordinary Shinra infantryman in Final Fantasy VII. It has two attacks: Machine Gun and Hand Grenade. They are more powerful than previous Shinra infantrymen encountered as they throw grenades at the party member with the lowest current HP, but are still not strong enemies. Grenade Combatant can use Hand Grenade up to four times before running out. They can also be fought during the return to Midgar at the end of the game, but at this point they are harmless.

The Gun Carrier is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII in the Underwater Reactor. It only has physical attacks. His Normal Shell attack may it use against each party members in one turn. About his Abnormal Shell attack always inflicts Slow and Darkness on one character. It drops large amounts of gil.

The Gun Bull Head is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. Just like any other robotic or machine foes, Gun Bull Head is vulnerable to magical attacks, taking half damage from Thunder; Fire or Ice work well. Due to Gun Bull Head being a slow enemy, Zack can run behind and use any physical attacks or Vital Slash or Blast Wave.

The Gunner's Gauntlet is a minigame in Final Fantasy X-2, played in Besaid. Orchestrated by Beclem, Yuna runs the gauntlet to prove to him that summoners are not worthless in a Spira without aeons. The reward for beating Beclem's score in the original mission, "Run the Gunner's Gauntlet", is the Enigma Plate Garment Grid. To start the minigame, the player must speak to Beclem standing close to the save sphere on the Village Slope. Datto takes his place in Chapter 5. There are two areas where the player can run the gauntlet: from the Village Slope to the Beach, or inside Besaid Temple's Cloister of Trials after Chapter 3. The time limit is 12 minutes and there is no direct reward for finishing the gauntlet, only what the player can find in treasure chests. Reaching the maximum level on Gunner's Gauntlet in the Final Fantasy X-2 HD Remaster will unlock the silver trophy The Gunner. __TOC__
(R).]] Gunromaru is a recurring katana in the Final Fantasy series.

Gunbreaker is a tank disciple of war job in Final Fantasy XIV introduced in the Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers expansion. Like most jobs introduced after A Realm Reborn, it has no base class, starting at level 60 and can be unlocked by completing the quest offered by a Gods' Quiver bow in New Gridania (X 11.5, Y 11.9).

The Haniel is an enemy from Final Fantasy III, fought in the Cave of Shadows. It divides into two when hit by a weapon other than a Dark Blade or inflicted with Paralysis. Therefore, bringing an Ancient Sword helps with dealing with these enemies for non-Dark Knights. They are moderately powerful otherwise, like all enemies in the cave.
Hammer Blaster is an enemy in Final Fantasy VII fought in Shinra Bldg. They can also be fought during the return to Midgar at the end of the game, but at this point they are harmless.
The Hammer Goblin is an enemy from Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Ring of Fates.
Hammerhead is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.
Hayne, also called the Dawn Shield, is a new character introduced in Final Fantasy Awakening. He is a student at Rubrum Academy.
Healing Helm , also known as Heal, is a recurring helmet in the Final Fantasy series.
.]] Heat Blaster is a recurring ability in the Final Fantasy series. It is an ability primarily used by Rikku.
The Headguard is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that slightly boosts the wearer's magickal defense and HP. It is the third weakest light armor hat in the game and basic equipment.

The Heavy Tank is an enemy in Final Fantasy VII. It is the only enemy fought at the site of the ruined mako reactor in Gongaga, and is also fought in the third round of the Battle Square during the time Tiny Bronco is available. While it might look intimidating, it is only a moderately powerful monster and should pose little threat to the party. When fought in the Battle Square its stats are enhanced with double the regular HP, and its Attack and Magic Attack are increased by 25%. The Heavy Tank morphs into Power Sources, useful for min-maxing.

The Heavy Shield, also styled as Heavy Shld, is the weakest heavy shield in Final Fantasy VI. The difference between heavy and universal shields is that only certain characters can equip the former, but they tend to have higher defensive stats than universal shields, though lack some of the universal shields' elemental etc properties. The Heavy Shield can be equipped by Terra, Locke, Edgar, Cyan, Celes, and Setzer to provide 22 defense, 14 magic defense, and 10 evasion. Betting the Heavy Shield in the Dragon's Neck Coliseum will pit the player against Typhon.

Heavy-Duty Bracer is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It has good stats and three single materia slots. It provides +53 to and +13 to . It is good to equip for physical protection and is the best physical defense armor at the time it becomes available.

Helletic Hojo is a boss in Final Fantasy VII during "Mako Cannon Rampage". Once the party defeats Hojo's human form, he transforms into Helletic Hojo, a hideous mass of writhing flesh still wearing his tattered lab coat and glasses. The boss theme for the battle is "J-E-N-O-V-A". __TOC__
The Helmet Heads are an enemy in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers.

The Heroic Shield is a shield in Final Fantasy III. It provides 10 Defense, 12 Magic Defense, and 12% Evasion in the 2D versions, and in the 3D versions, 9 Defense, 6 Magic Defense, and +1 to all stats. In all versions, it provides immunity to Petrify and Sleep. It can be used by the Onion Knight, Warrior, Knight, and [[Dragoon (Final Fantasy III)|Dragoon] classes, and in the 3D versions, the Freelancer class.

Hojo is a boss in Final Fantasy VII encountered near the control area of the Sister Ray at the end of "Mako Cannon Rampage". Cloud and his party arrive right as he is about to launch the giant cannon. This is the first part of a three-part battle. Hojo and all his transformations can be fought twice via the repeating boss glitch.

The Holy Miter is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a late game hat for mages, and is their best stat-boosting headgear, giving bonuses to Magic and Spirit on level up. The Holy Miter teaches the passive abilities Body Temp and Insomniac, which inoculate against status ailments.

The Horned Hat is a low to mid-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 10 and HP by 50. It is the fifth weakest light armor hat in the game and basic equipment.
Hunter's Longbow is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.

The Ice Lizard, also known as the IceLiz or Ice Liz, is an enemy in Final Fantasy IV. Cecil's Flame Sword is an extremely useful weapon, as is Tellah's Fira spell and Fire Arrows. It usually appears in groups of two with another enemy. The Complete Collection sprite of Ice Lizard resembles the Catoblepas from the iOS/Android version of Final Fantasy II.
.]] Ice Blade Renzan is a recurring ability in the Final Fantasy series. It is exclusively used by Kurasame Susaya in his spin-off appearances.

The Icecloud Arrows are ammunition for bows in Final Fantasy XII. They make the bow-user deal ice damage, able to exploit favorable weather conditions and enemy weakness. Bows cannot be equipped without owning some kind of arrows. Owning the Icecloud Arrows means the player can use an unlimited amount, and arrows do not need a license to be equipped alongside a bow. The Icecloud Arrows is the penultimate arrow set, below the Artemis Arrows.
Imperial Gunner is an enemy in Final Fantasy XII found in Archadian airships. They have low defenses, but shield themselves behind stronger soldiers. Their gun attacks ignore Defense.

Imdugud is a Rare Game enemy found in Nam-Yensa Sandsea in Final Fantasy XII. It is a stronger version of Zu. The player can steal the Shielded Armor from it. Imdugud is a flying enemy, so the party must use ranged weapons (and/or poles, rods and spears in Zodiac versions), magick, or long range Technicks, such as Telekinesis. It is also fought optionally in the Zodiac versions' Trial Mode Stage 8 alongside six Bagolys, where it appears if the player idles in the circular area where the Bagolys are. In the Trial Mode, it usually drops motes, but very rarely drops an Elixir. At the Trial, the player can steal a Killer Bow (common), Sirius (uncommon) and Paramina Crossbow (rare) from it, and poach it into Eksir Berries or a Hastega Mote.

The Imperial Rifleman is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought in various main quests and randomly appearing from assault craft. The bestiary describes them as cyborgs, as opposed to the magitek troopers that are fully machines. They are members of the imperial infantry. In the Japanese localization, the Imperial Rifleman's name is the name as the Imperial Trooper; the two enemies are largely interchangeable.

The Indurate Staff is a weapon for Sonon Kusakabe in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It teaches the Fighting Spirit ability, which causes Sonon's AI to focus on attacking the target. The Indurate Staff is geared towards physical attacks, having a significantly higher bonus than any other weapon in "Episode INTERmission", as well as rapid, albeit rather expensive, growth. However, its is lacking, and it provides little other than raw power. It is a good weapon for getting most out of Synergized Art of War.

The Interdimensional Train, also known as the Ghost Train or Subway, is a transportation device utilized by several characters in Final Fantasy: Unlimited. It is one of Cid's inventions, which he names Elizabeth (; alternatively spelled Elizabete in some English promotional materials). It is repeatedly attacked by Omega, in an attempt to retake the fragment that drives the train, and allows it to pass from world to world.

Interlude: Episode 1 is the first quest in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. It is the first of six interlude episodes in which the player controls Zack Fair. Zack carries Cloud Strife to Midgar's Sector 5, where a reporter broadcasts from the Midgar Expressway regarding heavy damage to the city caused by a tornado. Seeing Aerith Gainsborough among those unconscious in the tornado remains, Zack rushes off to the evacuating helicopters to find her.

The Invisibility Scroll, also known as Inviz Edge , is a throwing weapon in Final Fantasy VI, only usable via Shadow's or Gogo's Throw command. It bestows the thrower with invisibility, letting them become immune to physical attacks but vulnerable to magic, leading to the infamous Vanish-Doom bug in the earlier versions of Final Fantasy VI. Betting the Invisibility Scroll in the Dragon's Neck Coliseum will pit the player against Typhon.

The Iron Hammer is a hammer in Final Fantasy XII. It is the weakest hammer. In the Zodiac versions it is significantly weaker and obtained much earlier to complement the job system. In the original version, its license costs 15 LP. In the Zodiac versions, its license costs 25 LP, and it can be used by the Foebreaker.

Jade Weapon is an enemy in the Weapon Mode of Before Crisis -Final Fantasy VII-. Chronologically the first of the planet's Weapons to be awakened from beneath the ice, the Jade Weapon possesses approximately 3,000,000 HP. Around 200 meters in length, the Weapon generates a dark mist as it moves, enabling the Player Turks to track it through a radar system.

Ithuno is a Rare Game enemy in Final Fantasy XII found in the Barheim Passage. Its a stronger version of Mimeo. It is the source of the strongest weapon during the early gameplay, the Deathbringer sword.

Jamar Armor is a boss in Final Fantasy VII. It is the Proud Clod's chest piece, a mecha created and piloted by Scarlet and Heidegger. Its sole purpose is to allow the Proud Clod access the Materia-Jammer ability, and it has no attacks of its own. It is recommended to destroy the armor regardless, as it awards more EXP and AP than the Proud Clod itself, and also holds just as much gil, which is not awarded if the Proud Clod was defeated first. The player should use physical attacks, such as 2x Cut, and spells that hit all targets, such as Magic Breath. Jamar Armor most likely acts as the entry hatch into the machine itself, as it opens up when Heidegger and Scarlet emerge from inside the Proud Clod.

Jagidbod of Clan Reaper is a mission boss from Final Fantasy XI: Rise of the Zilart. He is encountered in San d'Oria Mission 7-2: The Secret Weapon, alongside Darokbok of Clan Reaper, Derakbak of Clan Wolf, the Reaper Clan Warmachine, and the Wolf Clan Warmachine.

The Jade Gown is a mid to high-ranked mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 44 (Zodiac) or 33 (original), and Magick Power by 8. In the Zodiac versions, it also gives 53 MP.

The Item Transmuter is a feature and key item in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, which allows players to craft items, armor, and accessories by combining multiple items together. Accessed from the menu after Broden gifts the party the transmuter in Kalm in chapter 2, "A New Journey Begins", players can craft new items that they have learned recipes for. Recipes for items are both earned by earning Transmuter XP (which is earned by crafting new items for the first time), and by finding transmuter chips via Excavation Intel.

Jenova∙BIRTH, referred to as Jenova-Birth in the BradyGames guide, is a boss from Final Fantasy VII. It attacks the party on the Cargo Ship from Junon to Costa del Sol at the climax of "Dangerous Voyage". It is possible to perform the repeating boss glitch with Jenova∙BIRTH.
Jobless is the placeholder "job" in Final Fantasy Dimensions. Their selection of equipment encompasses all or nearly all available weapons and armor.

Judge Ghis is a storyline boss in Final Fantasy XII. The party engages him on board the Dreadnought Leviathan. Three Imperial Swordsmen fight alongside him. Ghis is fought alongside the other Archadian Judges on Stage 100 of the Trial Mode in the Zodiac versions, where the Circlet can be stolen from him.
Zargabaath is a boss in the Zodiac versions of Final Fantasy XII fought in Trial Mode at Stage 100, alongside Gabranth, Drace, Bergan, and Ghis. A Grand Armor can be stolen from him.

The Judicer's Staff is a staff in Final Fantasy XII. It has a chance of inflicting Stop on-hit. In the original version, its license costs 30 LP. In the Zodiac versions its license costs 65 LP and it can be used by the Black Mage.

The Judo Uniform is a mid game light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX that everyone but Steiner and Freya can wear. It teaches Distract, which has enemies miss against the character more often, and HP+10%. The Judo Uniform provides a bonus to the wearer's Strength and Spirit when they level up with it equipped. The uniform is missable, but has no unique abilities and is not needed for synthesis.

Jury-Rigged Cutter is a boss in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It is a mecha deployed fought as part of the "Shears' Counterattack" odd job in Chapter 9, "The Town That Never Sleeps", in Corneo Colosseum. The player faces it when doing Madam M's quests for Cloud's dress. It can also be fought as part of the "Two-Person Team vs. Team Payback" round in Chapter 14, "In Search of Hope".
The Kactuar is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It has sky high Vitality but very low HP. A few standard sword slashes will quickly bring it down.
Ketill is a non-playable character in Final Fantasy XIV. Introduced at the end of Dawntrail. He is the airship captain of the Glaðr.
The Kilimweave Shirt is a low-ranked mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 8 and Magick Power by 3, and in the Zodiac versions, MP by 16.

The Knight Armor is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 12 Defense, 7 Magic Defense and 9% Evasion in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions it provides 25 Defense, 7 Magic Defense, and immunity to Petrify and Sleep. It can be used by the Onion Knight and Knight classes in all versions, and the Freelancer class in the 3D versions.

.]] Kuja's Outfit , also known as Kuja's Raiments and Kuja's Attire , is a recurring armor in the Final Fantasy series. It is the outfit most commonly worn by Kuja. Kuja first appeared as a character in Final Fantasy IX where he is not playable and where outfits are not equipment; Kuja's Outfit has since appeared as collectible armor in gacha games.

Lakkam is a blitzball player for the Al Bhed Psyches, occupying a defensive position. She can be found running up and down a corridor of the airship, outside the room where the rest of her teammates hang out.
The Laser Gun is a boss in Final Fantasy VI. It is the upper right portion of Air Force.

The Last Arm, also known as the Optic Blaster, is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV fought inside the Giant of Babil. It is recommended to hit the Last Arm with the party's most powerful attacks, such as Rydia using Bahamut or Leviathan, and Fusoya using Flare or Holy, to avoid it inflicting Stop on the entire party, making it that much more annoying to deal with.

Last Train is the ninth quest of Chapter 2, "Fateful Encounters", in Final Fantasy VII Remake. After escaping through the Sector 8 Business District, Cloud Strife leaps down onto the train, where he meets up with Avalanche.
The League Fighter is an enemy in Final Fantasy X-2. They are of no threat as they are simple to defeat and can only physically attack.
The League Veteran is an enemy in Final Fantasy X-2. His only method of attack is swinging his sword, so he should not pose that much of a threat.

.]] The Leather Suit , also known as AC Style is a recurring outfit in the Final Fantasy series. It first appears in Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children and is worn by Tifa Lockhart. The Leather Suit is composed of mostly black leather, a white tank-top under a black vest with a zipper going up the center, black leather overhauled shorts with a long cape at the back of Tifa's waist and black gloves. She wears dark boots and Tifa's hair is shorter than it was in Final Fantasy VII, reaching mid-back. A small pink ribbon is wrapped around her left bicep in memory of Aerith Gainsborough.

The Leather Hat is the basic light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is the weakest hat that everyone but Steiner and Freya can wear. The player can replace it as soon as they gain something better, as it does not contain any unique abilities. It can be used in synthesis.

The Leather Shirt is an early game light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX that everyone but Steiner and Freya can wear. It teaches Protect Girls, which lets Zidane take damage instead of female allies. The Leather Shirt is used in synthesis.
The Leather Breastplate is a light armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's defense by 6 and HP by 30. It is the third weakest light armor in the game and basic equipment.
The Leather Helm is a heavy armor helm in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 5 and Strength by 2. It is the weakest helm and basic equipment.

The Leather Bracer is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It prioritizes physical defense over magical defense, and has two unlinked materia slots. Its complement piece is the Mesmeric Armlet. The Leather Bracer provides +26 to and +6 to . It is good to replace the early equipment purchasable from Sector 7 slums.

Left Arm, referred to as Carry Armor Left Arm in the BradyGames guide, is a part of the Carry Armor boss found in Final Fantasy VII. It, along with the Right Arm, is able to pick a character up and damage them in battle, and Carry Armor needs an arm to conduct physical attacks.
Left Blade, otherwise known as LeftBladeand L. Blade, is a boss in Final Fantasy VI. It is the larger blade of Number 128 and is the left blade from 128's perspective.
Legendary Weapon is a Notorious Monster from Final Fantasy XI: Rise of the Zilart. It is spawned alongside Ancient Weapon for Zilart Mission 5: Headstone Pilgrimage.

The Light Temple is a location from Final Fantasy Mystic Quest. It can only be reached by warping from Kaidge Temple. After rescuing Captain Mac on his ship and having Phoebe join you. Before heading out to Doom Castle via Mac's Ship, you can meet the old man one last time in the Light Temple. He'll exchange words with Benjamin and fully restore their HP/MP before leaving.

Lieutenant Hamilton is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0 appearing in the second chapter mission "Operation Reconquista". He pilots a Prometheus magitek armor, and as such shares a Rubicus entry with it and the same moveset.

The Light Machine Gun is a gun-arm for Barret in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It teaches the Lifesaver ability, a crucial ability for Barret that causes him to take damage intended for other party members. The light machine gun provides a higher bonus than bonus, though it provides many unlocked abilities that nonetheless boost Barret's physical damage and durability. It also provides a decent number of materia slots. The gun looks like a machine gun converted into a gun arm. It is red, gray, and beige. It seems to have many aiming features to improve accuracy. The gun's barrel has slits to avoid overheating. It has two magazines, fitting with the in-game description.

The Light Woven Shirt is a mystic armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's Defense by 5 and Magick Power by 2, and in the Zodiac versions, MP by 7. It is the second weakest mystic armor in the game.

Lightning Eater is an auto-ability for armor in Final Fantasy X. Customized onto an armor's slot for 20 Lightning Gems, it absorbs all lightning-elemental damage the user takes as healing, even if they were a zombie. Lightning Eater is the upgraded version of Lightningproof, and takes priority over Lightningproof and Lightning Ward.

The Living Dead, also known as StillGoing, is an undead enemy in Final Fantasy VI, fought on the Phantom Train. Their special attack, Sapping Touch, inflicts sap on a party member, but otherwise they are very weak enemies who only use physical attacks and pose no threat.
The Long Arm is a boss in Final Fantasy VI fought as part of the first tier of the Statue of the Gods, a gauntlet leading up to the final boss, alongside Short Arm and Visage.
Luc Sardarc is a character from Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. He was a partner of the blade master Frimelda Lotice.

Lostwing is a village in Final Fantasy XVI, located in Central Sanbreque inside Fallen ruins known as an "airship", hence the name of the town. The town leader is Quinten, an ally to Cidolfus Telamon and the latter's quest to emancipate Bearers. Lostwing is known for its vineyards, but is rarely visited by anyone but traders who seek the village's fine wine since the road through Sanbreque around these parts has fallen to disuse.

Luxollid is a Rare Game enemy found in the Subterra of Pharos in Final Fantasy XII. The player can steal a good weapon from it, though which weapon it is depends on version. The player must kill the rare enemy Vagrant Soul in Abyssal-North, and then head to Umbra-South without saving or leaving the Subterra. Luxollid will spawn in the easternmost room of the southwestern corridor leading away from the Umbra-Interior. It is also fought in the Zodiac versions' Trial Mode at Stage 79 along with two Diakon Entites where a Dark Matter can rarely be stolen from it.

MAX attacks is a special type of attack in Final Fantasy Adventure. They vary depending on the current equipped weapon. When the Attack Gauge at the bottom of the screen is full, Sumo can unleash a MAX attack of the current equipped weapon. The MAX attack differs with each type of weapons: the character spins or charges with the sword, throws the axe or the spear, and gains capacity to attack in a wider range with chain-type weapons. MAX attack for physical attacks is twice the normal damage while for magic spells, the amount of damage is 4 times to normal damage.

MA Veles is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought in imperial bases, randomly dropped from assault craft (Chapter 5 onwards), and during the main quests The Power of Kings, The Hexatheon's Blessing, and The Trial of Ramuh. It is a magitek armor.
MA Veles-Bis is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought in Formouth Garrison and randomly dropped from landing craft.

MA Hoplomachus is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV found in Formouth Garrison and randomly dropped from assault craft. During the events of Assassin's Festival, Loqi Tummelt fought the party piloting this type of magitek armor. A corroded version of the Hoplomachus appears in Insomnia in the Windows and Royal Editions.

MA-X Cuirass is a boss in Final Fantasy XV. A magitek armor piloted by Loqi Tummelt, it is fought during the main quest Declaration of War and the sidequest Formouth Garrison. Loqi used a different MA during Final Fantasy XV: Assassin's Festival.

MA-X Patria is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV, randomly dropped from imperial landing craft. Because they spawn randomly, the player may end up fighting one in an early chapter, but it is fairly rare and its appearance is random. It is also faced as a mini-boss in the Adventurer from Another World collaboration quest with Final Fantasy XIV added in patch 1.27.

MA-X Dux is a boss in Final Fantasy XV. A magitek armor piloted by Caligo Ulldor, it is fought during the sidequest Formouth Garrison. Ulldor uses a different MA, the MA-X Aureus, in Final Fantasy XV: Episode Ignis.
MA-X Aureus is a boss in Final Fantasy XV: Episode Ignis. It is a golden magitek armor piloted by Caligo Ulldor.

The Magepower Shishak is a top-tier heavy armor helm in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 47 (Zodiac) or 39 (original), Strength by 11 and—unusually for a heavy armor helm—Magick Power by 5, the latter making it good for a katana-wielder. The Magepower Shishak is metallic for the purposes of the magnetize debuff present during the Vinuskar (though mainly available after this boss) and Ultima boss battles.

The Mage Robe is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 9 Defense, 7 Magic Defense, and 7% Evasion in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions it provides 13 Defense, 13 Magic Defense, +1 Intellect, and +1 Mind. It can be used by the Onion Knight, White Mage, Black Mage, Scholar, Geomancer, Evoker, Bard, Devout, Magus, Summoner, and Sage classes in all versions, and the Freelancer class in the 3D versions.

The Magic Vice is an enemy from Final Fantasy IX found in the Burmecia Suburbs. They can be difficult to deal with when they use Magic Hammer to deplete a magic-using character's MP. When at critical health, the Magic Vice will often flee the battle. Like the standard Vice, Magic Vice can steal items from the party with Mug. Any stolen items are lost forever, even if the Magic Vice is subsequently defeated. This can be of considerable inconvenience as the only way to recover these items is to load a previous save file.

Magitek Axeman is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV, fought during several quests and randomly dropped from imperial landing craft. The Level 6 version can be fought with Cor as a guest. The Level 6 Magitek Axeman is the quintessential magitek trooper, its model representing them in Final Fantasy XV: Episode Prompto and Final Fantasy XV: Assassin's Festival, and models like it appearing in Kingsglaive: Final Fantasy XV.

Magitek Bannerman is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought around the map after arriving in random landing craft drops. The early level versions can be missed for bestiary completion if the player does not encounter them in time, as they only appear in the early chapters (see below).

Magitek Swordsman is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought randomly around the map from assault craft, and during various main quests. It is a magitek trooper that wields a sword and has an built-in firearm in its hand.
Magitek Assassin is an enemy in Final Fantasy XV fought randomly throughout the map from landing craft drops, and during the sidequest Formouth Garrison. It is a magitek trooper.
